clue.text: Using iron is vital

definitions.meaning: running a hot iron over clothes to smooth them

explanation.definitionFit: Ironing clothes is pressing them, and an urgent matter is a pressing one.

clue.text: Prepare staple dishes

indicators.note: to prepare something is to work it into shape, so the letters of staple are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook gets the basic dishes ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staple dishes' reads as basic food, but 'staple' is the fodder that 'Prepare' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates are the flat dishes food is served on.

clue.text: Politician in Ireland given supreme power

indicators.note: the politician sits inside the word for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An Irish politician is handed total control.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm under sovereign rule, so the word also stands for supreme dominion.

clue.text: Hidden and shown

definitions.meaning: displayed on a screen, as a film is

explanation.definitionFit: A screen can both conceal something behind it and display a film on it, giving opposite senses.

clue.text: No Greek character is other than superior

parts.note: taken as written
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is said to have no character beyond a sense of superiority.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels coined in 1950s Britain for upper-class and not upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U was British slang for behaviour or speech not typical of the upper class.

clue.text: Neglect can make a ninny turn to drink

indicators.note: the word for a ninny is turned round, read from its end

parts.note: a sap is a foolish person
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Neglect can drive a fool to the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses SAP to give PAS, then SUP follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up an opportunity is to forgo or ignore it.

clue.text: A bawdy-sounding advert

indicators.note: the clue words are to be spoken, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: a lewd, bawdy meaning lewd

explanation.surface: An advertisement that sounds a bit smutty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advert' is not an advertisement here but the formal verb meaning to refer to something.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to a subject is to refer to it indirectly, the same as hinting at it.

clue.text: Seek tall models with extremely slim figures

indicators.note: as a verb, models means shapes or forms, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion agency hunts for tall catwalk models who are extremely thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like the catwalk noun but is a verb signalling the rearrangement of SEEK TALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone painfully thin looks like a bare skeleton, all bones.

clue.text: Claims an old city quarter will provide a diversion

parts.note: pleas are claims or appeals
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone claims that a district of an ancient city offers entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversion is an amusement, something done for enjoyment.

clue.text: A quiet family man, that's obvious

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a parent heads a family

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken father is clearly what he seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is plain to see, evident.

clue.text: A French article about support, say

indicators.note: the French article goes round the support

parts.note: le is a French word for the
a leg is a supporting post, as of a table

explanation.surface: A French grammar point is said to concern a prop.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or claim something, often without proof.

clue.text: The listener must be involved in subtle but all-in fashion

indicators.note: the listener is wrapped up inside the word for subtle

parts.note: wily means cunning or subtle
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A listener must take part in some subtle but exhausting style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-in' is British for exhausted, so 'all-in fashion' means in a tired manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a worn-out way is doing it tiredly.

clue.text: Highly inaccessible retreats for high-fliers

parts.note: the high-fliers are birds of prey, whose nests are built on lofty crags

explanation.definitionFit: Eagles and other raptors build their nests on high, hard-to-reach ledges.

clue.text: Put off deals-she is without capital

indicators.note: put off suggests being disturbed or upset, so the letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: She deals, but a broke dealer is deterred from playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without capital' means lacking a head, capital meaning head (as in capital punishment).
explanation.definitionFit: Capital comes from the Latin for head, so lacking a capital is lacking a head.

clue.text: A male in a store may appear embarrassed

indicators.note: the pair of letters sits inside the word for a store

parts.note: a shed is a storage hut

explanation.surface: A man in a shop may look awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's first A goes inside SHED with M; the second A ('a store') stands at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Being embarrassed is feeling shame or awkwardness.

clue.text: A point will be seen in due course

indicators.note: the compass point appears inside the word for due

parts.note: one's deserts are what one is due, as in just deserts
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A point will become clear eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in due course' reads as 'eventually', but 'course' is the definition, a stage of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudding is the sweet course served at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Mean to grab one or two

indicators.note: the average seizes the numeral, holding it inside

parts.note: par is the average or norm
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stingy person tries to grab one or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple, or a brace, is a set of two.

clue.text: He's personally decorated

parts.note: read as a man who decorates persons, applying ink designs to their skin, rather than one wearing medals

explanation.definitionFit: A body artist ornaments people's skin with inked designs.

clue.text: Delightful-could start doing damage though

indicators.note: the start of the word could is its opening letter

parts.note: harming means injuring or damaging

explanation.surface: Something delightful could start to do harm after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming means pleasing, attractive.

clue.text: Come together, opposing some plot

parts.note: con is against, as in pros and cons
a tract is an area or plot of land

explanation.surface: People unite, opposing a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To contract is to shrink or draw together.

clue.text: A cheerful expression may well hide pain

indicators.note: the letters sit concealed within the words a cheerful

explanation.surface: A cheerful expression may conceal hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent dull pain is called an ache.

clue.text: This gets blown up when everyone is in favour

indicators.note: everyone sits inside the word for favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Something gets inflated when everyone is in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A party balloon is inflated by blowing air into it.

clue.text: Possibly remain at sea

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of remain could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A sailor might stay out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine describes what is of or on the ocean.

clue.text: Top Venetian's responsibility to see an animal fed

parts.note: a dog is an animal
ate means fed, took food

explanation.surface: A Venetian ruler's duty is to see an animal is fed.
explanation.walkthrough: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice; his office is the dogate.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or term of the doge, who ruled Venice, is called the dogate.

clue.text: Express contrition when imprisoned again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
pent, as in pent up, means confined

explanation.surface: A prisoner shows remorse on being locked up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel and show sorrow for wrongdoing is to show contrition.

clue.text: Housing for caterers perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that caterers could be rearranged

explanation.surface: Accommodation provided for catering staff, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRACES are British rows of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, so terraces are a form of housing.

clue.text: Holy man had transport but went on foot

parts.note: St, saint, is a holy man
rode means travelled on a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A saint had a ride but walked instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride is to walk with long steps, and that verb's past tense is the answer.

clue.text: In the jungle each new plant gives joy

indicators.note: the letters are found in the words jungle each

explanation.surface: Each new plant in the jungle is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is great delight.

clue.text: Big bloomer made by a revered figure in ancient Egypt

definitions.text: a revered figure in ancient Egypt

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
an iris is a flowering plant, something that blooms

explanation.surface: An enormous blunder made by a respected Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian god of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Rent allowance cut in tame bird's home

indicators.note: the shortened allowance goes inside the bird's home

parts.note: a pet bird lives in a cage

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: leave is permission or allowance

explanation.surface: A rent allowance is reduced inside a pet bird's cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' is not money paid but a noun meaning a split or tear; 'cut' trims LEAVE to LEAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a split or division, like a tear.

clue.text: Digger oddly dressed

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters come out in a strange order

explanation.surface: A digger in strange clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigged ship is fitted out with sails, dressed for sea.

clue.text: People in singlet, casual shirt, or formal wear

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the garments

parts.note: a vest is a singlet
T, short for T-shirt
men are people

explanation.surface: People in undershirts or casual tops, or in formal attire.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe, especially one worn by clergy.
